decisions.reason: The causal-overclaim allegation is false: the Definition expressly supplies a population observed-law functional, while the separate IPW identification theorem supplies consistency, exchangeability, positivity and integrable potential outcomes. Independently, the digest correctly identifies the sentence calling e_a the weight: the displayed integrand and instructions use I_a/e_a. Corrected that sentence alone; no formula or admissibility condition changed.

The title describes the intended application, while the Definition explicitly defines only the observed-law standardization functional. Indicator integrability and positivity give the conditional classes q_a,e_a and their a.s. ratio; integrability of that ratio is expressly required for the output. No equality with E[Y^a] is asserted here: thm-standardization-identifies-a-causal-mean and the owning page separately state consistency, conditional exchangeability and target integrability. Adding these assumptions to a purely observed-law procedure is unnecessary.

Replaced only the erroneous description of e_a as the outcome weight by I_a/e_a. Causal equality remains a separate theorem with explicit full-data hypotheses; this is a local repair review, not independent acceptance of my edit.

Reviewed the complete procedure, all six actual prerequisite definitions, its contract and page, and the separate standardization identification argument. The q_a/e_a construction uses a.s. conditional-expectation classes under inherited AC; q_a exists since I_aY is integrable, the denominator is positive a.s., and the expressly required ratio integrability ensures a finite output independent of versions. The finite-stratum sum agrees with this procedure. Causal assumptions belong to the separate identification theorem, so the rejection supplies no defect and the item remains unchanged.
